title: T-REX: A 68-to-567µs/Token 0.41-to-3.95µJ/Token Transformer Accelerator with Reduced External Memory Access and Enhanced Hardware Utilization in 16nm FinFET
problem: Transformer accelerators for inference typically suffer from external memory access (EMA) dominating energy (up to 81%), and low hardware utilization (as low as 9%), resulting in poor latency and energy efficiency despite optimized on-chip computation.
motivation: Recent analysis shows EMA is the primary energy bottleneck in transformer inference; improving memory subsystem and hardware utilization can deliver significant end-to-end energy and latency gains beyond compute optimization alone.
method: T-REX architecture reduces EMA via intelligent data reuse and memory hierarchy optimization; enhances hardware utilization through improved scheduling and dataflow; operates across token latency range 68-567µs depending on model/batch, achieving 0.41-3.95µJ/token energy.
key_novelty: First transformer accelerator design explicitly targeting external memory access reduction as primary optimization goal, demonstrating that memory subsystem efficiency and utilization can dominate performance gains over traditional on-chip compute optimization.
contributions: Reduced external memory access (EMA) through optimized data reuse and memory hierarchy
Enhanced hardware utilization overcoming prior 9% bottleneck
68-567 µs/token latency range supporting diverse inference scenarios

metrics.other: Up to 81% EMA reduction vs prior designs

baselines: Prior encoder-only transformer accelerators with quantization/sparsity/pruning optimization; references 4 achieving 9% utilization
limitations: Specific transformer model sizes, batch configurations, and detailed utilization percentages not provided; comparison with other recent accelerators (refs 1-7) not quantified.
